source.title: CGHS rates applicable for treatment at healthcare organisation — Office Memorandum F.No.5-16/CGHS(HQ)/HEC/2024(Part I), Directorate General of CGHS, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, 3 October 2025 (effective 13 October 2025)
source.basis: Annexure-I Part A: semi-private ward rates for X (Tier I) cities, with the Non-NABH, NABH and Super-speciality columns as printed. Parts B and C (Tier II and III) were read too: every one of the 1,995 codes with three entries is exactly 90% and 80% of its Tier I rate, which is how the tier multipliers below were confirmed.
source.curated: 240 everyday items chosen from 1,995 codes; the full list is in the OM. Names are verbatim from the OM.
source.caveat: CGHS rates bind CGHS-empanelled hospitals for CGHS beneficiaries. For a private patient they are a public reference point, not a cap: private tariffs are lawful, and a hospital must display its own rates (Clinical Establishments (Central Government) Rules 2012, Rule 9(i)) in the states that have adopted the Act. Use the range to decide which lines to question, never to refuse payment.

I.label: X (Tier I)
I.note: Urban agglomerations as per Department of Expenditure O.M. No.2/5/2017-E.II(B), 7 July 2017.

II.label: Y (Tier II)
II.note: Indicative list in the OM; Tier II rates also apply in the North-East region and the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

hospital.note: The OM prints three columns: Non-NABH/Non-NABL (15% below NABH), NABH/NABL, and Super-speciality (15% above NABH for the corresponding super specialities). Treatment at a non-empanelled private hospital is restricted to the Non-NABH rate of the city.

ward.note: Package rates are for the semi-private ward; general ward −5%, private ward +5%. Consultations, investigations, radiotherapy, day care and minor procedures stay uniform.
